attributes.description: Larger, closer targets are faster to hit. Drives 60px minimum target.
More choices = more time to decide. Drives max 5 items per screen, 2 top-level choices.
Working memory holds ~7 items. Drives max 5 items per screen and chunked line items.
Users expect sites to work like other sites they know. Borrow bank-statement and text-message patterns.
Complexity can't be removed, only moved. We move it from user to system; depth always reachable.
People remember the peak and the end of an experience. Every flow ends on an answer, never a dashboard.
Polished design is perceived as more usable. Visual quality IS the trust signal here.
Responses under 400ms eliminate user impatience. Capture-to-answer target is under 30 seconds.

attributes.why: 44 is a floor, not a target. Marguerite's reading glasses and Rafael's cracked screen set the bar. Apple itself uses 60pt on visionOS, so there is precedent. Exceeding a minimum is not a violation.

attributes.hig_default: System red for alerts and warnings
attributes.our_rule: **Red only for destructive confirmation.** Never for bill status.
attributes.why: Rafael has been targeted by shutoff scams. Alarm styling from us is indistinguishable from fraud to him. Bill status is carried in words, never colour.

attributes.our_rule: **No tab bar.** Home plus persistent Add.
attributes.why: Hick's Law. Five tabs is five decisions on every launch for a product with two real destinations.

attributes.our_rule: **19pt body text**, with full Dynamic Type support
attributes.why: 17 is correct for a general app. This one gets read once, slowly, by someone in reading glasses. Dynamic Type is Apple's native answer to accessibility without a bolt-on mode, which is exactly the universal design position.

attributes.consideration: Utility bills contain full name, service address, account number and payment history. PII with identity-theft value, not merely financial data.
The cloud fallback path sends bill imagery to a third party. Where it runs, what it retains, and how that is disclosed is product-defining, not a vendor choice.
Local-first is the architecture. Every design decision must preserve it, and any server-side component requires explicit re-approval.
Users may add bills in another person's name, legitimate for renters and family. We must never verify ownership, and must never allow this to become a surveillance mechanism.
US only. State privacy laws apply, notably CCPA/CPRA. Utility account data may carry additional state protections. Legal review before launch.
Export and deletion must be real and complete. Largely simplified by local-first, but the encrypted backup is now the surface that matters.
Encrypted local backup becomes the single point of data loss and the single most valuable artifact to steal. Key handling is critical.

attributes.description: All design tokens live in one global CSS/JS file. Edit one place, change everywhere. No inline styles.
Frontend (Flutter) and backend (Supabase + FastAPI) are in separate top-level folders. They talk via HTTP/REST.
All HIG tokens (60px targets, 19pt body, no-status-colour) are declared in lib/theme/ and injected via ThemeData.
The AI/OCR pipeline and the analytics dashboard are Python only. No model arithmetic — models narrate, code computes.
Language models never compute bill totals. Deterministic Python code does arithmetic. Models only read images and write sentences.
OAuth is wired but a BYPASS_AUTH env flag skips it so you can test without logging in.
Every table has RLS enabled. A user only reads rows where user_id matches their JWT.
Every extracted field stores a confidence score and a bounding-box region referencing the source image. Nothing displayed without a source.
Single codebase for Web, iOS, and Android. Renders Apple-HIG-inspired UI via custom ThemeData.
Postgres + Auth + Storage. Handles user accounts, bill data, image storage, and real-time sync.
REST microservice for OCR (image-to-text), bill parsing, and deterministic self-validation engine.
Google + Apple sign-in via Supabase Auth. Bypassed with BYPASS_AUTH flag in v1 for local testing.
Extracts raw text + bounding boxes from bill images. Feeds the bill-parsing AI layer.
Python dashboard for spend decomposition and usage analysis graphs.
Token vocabulary (radius, spacing, colour, motion) translated into Flutter ThemeData and global CSS variables for web.
